title: Uncle Bob is Ruining Software
summary: Hillel Wayne argues that 'best practices' flow from star programmers who would succeed with or without them, so authority is weak evidence and only research could tell which techniques work.

assertions.quote: We have no a priori way to determine whether a given practice is good or bad purely based on what the best programmers do

verdicts.note: The logic holds and practice adoption is visibly driven by prominent advocates, but how much of practice folklore actually originates this way is not measured.

assertions.quote: I can't look into the research because there's almost no software engineering research out there.
We could force 10x programmers to argue topics, which I'd like to see happen more- it isn't great but it helps a little

verdicts.note: A preference about discourse rather than a prediction that could be checked.
